newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton sees tough markets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton sees tough markets.

text.p: Cement producer Adelaide Brighton Ltd said on Monday it expects only a modest increase in profits in 1996/97 as there was no evidence of any improvement in the depressed construction markets in Australia or Hawaii.

"Because there is no evidence of any improvement in the depressed construction markets in Australia or Hawaii during the 1996/97 fiscal year, the board expects only a modest increase in profits," Adelaide Brighton said in its annual report.
Adelaide Brighton made a net loss of A$49.3 million for the year to June 30, 1996 after abnormal losses of A$62.6 million.

Adelaide Brighton said any increase in profits would be as a result of improvement to operations. "Most forecasters expect that the Australian building industry will show reasonable to strong growth from 1998-2000, and the company is well positioned to take advantage of this upturn," it said.
"The company has emerged leaner, more focused and stronger after a major restructuring of its investments, strategy, board, management and employees," Adelaide Brighton said.
Most of the company's abnormal losses in 1995/96 were related to its disasterous Gunpowder copper mine investment.
The company has said it will sell its investment in the pipe businesses of Humes Industries Ltd in New Zealand and is likely to sell its other New Zealand business, Hurricane Wire Products.
